title: Earn your keep
offer: Nobody here feeds a stranger twice. Catch five fish off the town pier and sell them to Delphine. Then we will talk about boats.
progressText: Fish caught at the Town Pier
done: Good. You can fish. That is one more thing than most people who wash up here.

title: A proper line
offer: That braided coconut string will get you killed, or worse, laughed at. Buy a mono line from Marisol and show me.
done: Now you look like you live here.

title: Something that floats on purpose
offer: I have a skiff in the yard that needs an owner. It is not free, but it is honest. Come back when it is yours.
progressText: Buy the skiff at the boatyard
done: She leaks a little at the transom. They all do. Mind the Cut on a falling tide.

title: The wreck
offer: That island you came from. There was a ship on its reef, before your time and mine. With the skiff you could get out to her. Go and look; bring back the story.
done: So she is still there. And so is he, I suppose: the old barracuda off the point. Bring me whatever she gives up.

title: The dock fish
offer: Start where everybody starts. Bring me word you have caught a gray snapper: they are under the pier, and they are cleverer than they look.
done: Shrimp, light line, patience. You are learning.

title: Something that pulls
offer: You want to know what a rod is for? Hook a crevalle jack. They come into the harbour at first and last light.
done: Ha! Your arm hurts. Good. That is the feeling I sell.

title: Bait that swims
offer: The serious fish want serious bait. Buy a cast net, throw it on the sardine school by the pier, and show me a live one.
done: Now you are dangerous. Hook it through the nose and it swims for an hour.

title: Linesider
offer: A snook of sixty centimetres. Under the lamp at night, or along the mangrove roots at dawn. I want to hear how it jumped.
progressText: Catch a snook of 60 cm or more
done: Three jumps? They always tell me three. Take this; you have earned a real lure.

title: Supper
offer: My teeth are not what they were, but a yellowtail snapper, fresh, I can still manage. Bring me one.
done: Ah. Sit. I will tell you about the black ones under the ledge.

title: The other shift
offer: You young people fish in the sun and go home. Catch three fish after dark and tell me the sea is the same place.
done: No. It is not the same place. Now you know.

title: One for the wall
offer: Any fool catches fish. Bring me word of a trophy: a fish big for its kind, any kind.
done: Measure it twice and tell it once. That is how records are kept.

title: The silver king
offer: There is one fish I never brought to the boat. You know which. Land a tarpon, let it go, and come and tell an old man what it felt like.
done: …Yes. That is what I thought it would be like. There is one more. I will tell Marisol to order you some real gear.

title: A tagged bonefish
offer: I am Imani Reyes; I study the flats fish for the university. Bonefish move between these cayes and nobody knows quite how. Catch one and let it go, and tell me where. Here is how I tag them.
done: Good. That fish will turn up in someone's data in a year. Keep the kit. Bonefish you may sell, but a tarpon or anything else the law protects has to go back, and I pay for every one of those you tag and release.

title: Night shift at the Cut
offer: Fish move through the Cut on the tide, and the tide follows the moon. Fish it after dark, three fish, and note what the water is doing.
progressText: Fish caught in the Cut after dark
done: Interesting. The big tides run hardest there. Tobias will tell you a story about that; it is mostly true.

title: Silver king
offer: Tarpon are the hardest fish to study and the easiest to love. Tag one for me. Anywhere.
done: Every tarpon tagged in this country is in a database, and now so is yours. And since you asked about the Bishop, every account of him agrees on the bait.

title: The grouper count
offer: Nassau grouper were the commonest big fish on this reef. Now we count them one at a time. If you catch one, measure it, release it, and tell me.
done: One more than last year's count. That is the best news I have had all month.

title: Further than the reef
offer: A man came through last month off a freighter from Belém. He said there is a river in Brazil the colour of coffee, with fish in it that tow canoes. You have the look of someone who would go. Get yourself a proper reel first, and I will find you a berth.
done: Good. I have written to a cousin of a cousin. The passage is on my board whenever you have the coins. Bring me back a story.

title: Off the planks
offer: Before I take anyone out, I watch them fish. Catch five fish off the floating houses, and sell them to Dona Socorro.
progressText: Fish caught at the Town Waterfront
done: You can fish. Your casting is terrible, but you can fish.

title: A boat of your own
offer: Nobody gets anywhere here without a canoe. I have one. It is a good one, with a rabeta that only stops when it wants to.
progressText: Buy the canoe at the boat landing
done: Now you can go anywhere. Not upriver, not yet. But anywhere. There is a biologist in town who will want to meet you.

title: Tucunaré
offer: Take the canoe to the island lagoon and catch me a butterfly peacock. Watch the water while you are there; you will see something you do not believe.
progressText: Catch a butterfly peacock bass at the Island Lagoon
done: Did you see it come up? The pirarucu. They used to fill that lagoon.

title: Upriver
offer: The real fish are two days up the tributaries, at the rapids. You need a river boat for that, with a cook and hammocks. I know a man who will sell one.
progressText: Buy a river boat at the boat landing
done: Now you are a real expedition. Watch the rocks below the falls, and do not swim in the plunge pool.

title: Your first tucunaré
offer: You cannot sell lures for a fish nobody has caught. Bring me a butterfly peacock, any size, from anywhere on the river.
done: There. Now you are ruined for every other fish. Take this; you will need it for the big ones.

title: Live bait
offer: The big fish here eat sardinha. Buy a cast net from me, throw it under the floating houses, and come back with live sardinha.
progressText: Catch live sardinha with a cast net
done: Now you have the bait every predator in the river wants. Use it upriver.

title: Açu
offer: The speckled peacock, the tucunaré-açu: that is why anglers fly here from the other side of the world. Catch one over sixty centimetres, and let it go.
progressText: Catch a speckled peacock bass over 60 cm
done: Sixty! You will lie about it for the rest of your life. Everybody does.

title: Eyes under the water
offer: The giants live where you cannot see: twenty metres down in the channel, and in the holes below the falls. Buy a fish finder and you will know where to drop a bait.
done: Now you will see them. Seeing them is not the same as landing them.

title: Who eats jaraqui
offer: There is a saying: whoever eats jaraqui never leaves. Bring me one. Throw a cast net under the planks; they do not take a hook.
done: Grilled on the fire, with farinha. Now you will never leave. Sit, I will tell you about the fish I have seen.

title: The river at night
offer: The river is a different place at night. The catfish come up. Catch three fish after dark, anywhere.
done: You see? At night the river belongs to the bigger mouths.

title: Something to remember
offer: Everyone catches fish. Catch me one worth remembering: a trophy, the kind you see twice in a year.
done: That one you will tell your grandchildren about. I was the same.

title: Pirarara
offer: One more. The pirarara, the redtail catfish. I lost one at the lagoon mouth when I was twenty, and I have not stopped thinking about it. Catch one.
done: Red tail, yellow belly, a head like a shovel. Yes. That is the one. Thank you.

title: Let them go
offer: Sport fishing in Amazonas is catch and release: that is the law, and it is why there are still big fish here. Show me. Release two butterfly peacocks.
done: Gently, wet hands, back in the water. You would be surprised how many people cannot do that.

title: Piaba
offer: This town lives partly on cardinal tetras, caught by hand in the forest streams and flown to aquariums all over the world. When people earn from the fish, they keep the forest. Bring me two bags.
progressText: Bring Dr Prado two bags of cardinal tetras
done: Bright as neon, every one. These go to the project tank.

title: The açu goes back
offer: Catch a speckled peacock bass and release it. I want to know where the big ones are this year.
done: Noted, measured, released. The breeding fish are what keep this river famous.

title: Pirarucu
offer: The arapaima. The pirarucu. It was fished nearly to nothing; now the communities manage it and count it every year. If you ever have one on, bring it to the side of the boat and let it go.
done: Two hundred kilos of fish that breathes air, back in its lake. Thank you. That one is in my count.
